title: Why We Have Popcorn at the Movies
paragraphs: Many people love to eat popcorn when they watch a movie at the cinema. But why do we eat popcorn at the movies? The answer goes back almost 100 years.

People have eaten popcorn for a very long time, and in the late 1800s it was already a popular snack at fairs and on city streets. In the early days of film, many cinemas did not want popcorn. At that time, cinemas wanted to be like fancy theaters, where people watched plays. Popcorn was seen as a messy snack, and owners did not want it on their nice carpets.

But things changed. When movies started to have sound in the late 1920s, many more people began to go to the cinema. Then, in the 1930s, the Great Depression began. Many people had very little money. But popcorn was cheap. A bag cost only 5 to 10 cents, so most people could buy it.

At first, people bought popcorn from sellers outside the cinema and brought it inside. Later, some cinema owners let sellers work in their lobbies if they paid a fee. Soon, many cinemas started selling popcorn themselves. During the Great Depression, cinemas were losing money, and popcorn helped them earn more.
During World War II, sugar was hard to get, so candy became more expensive. But popcorn stayed cheap. This made it even more popular.
Today, popcorn is still an important part of going to the movies. For many cinemas, selling snacks like popcorn is a very important way to make money.
